text.title: Regression Test First Bugfix Workflow — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete workflow record for a Sentry checkout bug (zero amount with a Turkish locale): inputs lifted from the payload, red test committed alone with its failing CI run, an 18-line fix, the green run, and the 90-day review against Sentry, with a note on each non-obvious value; then the same bug fixed the usual way and what the validator and the reviewer see.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Sentry issue ACME-SHOP-12345: `ValidationError: amount must be positive` on `POST /checkout` for a cart with `amount=0.0`, `locale=tr_TR`, `currency=TRY`. The breadcrumbs show an `Order` row written before the serializer rejected the request. swe:alice owns the fix; SLA is 24 hours, so there is time for the red run before shipping.

example.title: ACME-SHOP-12345 zero-amount checkout
example.note: `reproducing_inputs` carries `locale=tr_TR` and `amount=0.0` because those are the payload fields; a test with `en_US` and `9.99` would not have fired (r-inputs-lifted-from-alert-payload). The customer's email was replaced by a synthetic address of the same shape and the substitution is listed (same rule). `asserts[]` names the 422 and the message fragment from the alert, and `side_effect_asserts[]` checks that no `Order` row exists, because the breadcrumbs showed one being written (r-test-fails-for-the-alerts-reason). `commit` a1b2c3d is the test-only commit; CI run 76 is its failing run and `stable_runs: 3` records that it failed the same way three times (r-red-test-committed-before-fix, r-test-is-deterministic-and-located). `first_fix_commit` b2c3d4e is a different commit on top of it and the fix is 18 lines with the test file untouched (r-fix-is-minimal-and-assertions-untouched). Run 77 is the complete PR's green run, read from CI (r-ci-shows-red-then-green). `next_review_at` is 2026-05-24 plus 90 days, and on that day Sentry showed zero regression events and no new issue with the same signature, so `alert_resolved: true` stands (r-alert-closed-after-recurrence-window).

example.title: the same bug fixed the usual way
example.note: What the validator prints: `red_test.path` is not under `tests/regression/` and `stable_runs` is below 3 (r-test-is-deterministic-and-located); `commit_message_has_alert_url` is false (r-red-test-committed-before-fix); `asserts[0]` is `pytest.raises(Exception)` and `side_effect_asserts` is missing although `alert.side_effect` is set (r-test-fails-for-the-alerts-reason); `fix.touches_red_test_assertions` is true (r-fix-is-minimal-and-assertions-untouched); `next_review_at` is 31 days after `merged_at`, not 90 (r-alert-closed-after-recurrence-window); and, once those are fixed, the cross-field check finds `red_test.commit` equal to `fix.first_fix_commit`, so test and fix landed in one commit and nobody has seen the test fail (fm-test-written-after-fix). What the reviewer sees: the inputs are the developer's defaults, not the payload, so the test reproduces a hypothesis and the alert with `locale=tr_TR` keeps firing (fm-invented-repro-inputs); and a 412-line diff that also edits the test's assertions cannot be reverted alone (fm-assertion-edited-to-pass).
